A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ∇-GFlowNet study. Their text, equations, Table 1, Figures 1–31, and appendices A–J are available and support reliable comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original Stable Diffusion finetuning experiments on Aesthetic Score, HPSv2, and ImageReward, including quantitative comparisons, ablations, and generated samples.

after.justification: v2 retains the original quantitative experiments and appendix analyses, together with revised qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The ∇-DB and residual ∇-DB objectives, forward-looking parameterization, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The non-ideal-prior correction and prior-strength adaptation in the appendices already appear in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three reward tasks, 45-animal prompt collection, and HPDv2 photo/painting prompts. Replaced sample images retain the existing task and prompt coverage.

E2.justification: DDPO, ReFL, DRaFT-1, DRaFT-LV, DAG-DB, and residual DB retain their participation in corresponding comparisons. The comparator subsets in the appendix experiments also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 changes the stated temperature sweep from {5000, 7000, 1000} to {5000, 7000, 10000}. Figure 8 already shows 10000 in v1, indicating a correction to the reported setting rather than evidence of rerunning experiments. Other protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 3 replaces ReFL and DRaFT-LV examples illustrating training instability, and Appendix J replaces their examples in the qualitative diversity comparisons. These revise existing case-study evidence; the numerical sensitivity and ablation analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three random seeds and retain the same mean-and-standard-deviation reporting in Table 1 and convergence plots. No new uncertainty estimation or statistical testing is reported.

E6.justification: Figure 2 replaces baseline examples and changes their displayed average rewards: ReFL 6.31 to 6.67 and DRaFT-LV 6.98 to 6.69. Figures 3 and 27–31 also replace qualitative result entries. These are revised sample-based results; Table 1 and the quantitative curves remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The propositions, mathematical objectives, and appendix derivations are retained. Appendix B.3 expands its closing sentence to restate the already-proved zero-loss implication, without changing the assumptions or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a reward-gradient-informed GFlowNet objective and fast diffusion finetuning that preserves diversity and the pretrained prior. Added post-training/alignment terminology does not alter these contributions or their scope.

C2.justification: The interpretations of convergence, diversity, prior preservation, and training collapse remain unchanged, as do the ablation explanations. Appendix C retains the same caveat concerning bias with non-ideal pretrained models.

D1.justification: The corrected temperature value in Section 4.4 improves hyperparameter documentation by matching Figure 8. Architecture, LoRA rank, learning rates, sampling details, hardware disclosures, and project access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Six references are added. Section 2.2 explicitly connects detailed balance with soft Q-learning, path consistency learning, and maximum-entropy RL; Section 5 expands diffusion-sampler and prompt-adaptation context and removes the earlier broad contrast with RL. Core novelty positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: There are limited edits to the abstract, contribution wording, related-work discussion, and proof explanations, plus updated affiliations and conference headers. The section organization and overall narrative remain substantially the same.

P2.justification: Figures 2–3 and 27–31 contain replaced image panels, and some retained panels use higher-resolution images. Their comparison structures and captions remain stable. Other changes are limited to page flow and reference-list expansion.

improvement.justification: The temperature correction resolves an internal inconsistency between Section 4.4 and Figure 8, improving reproducibility documentation. The added maximum-entropy RL discussion provides clearer research positioning. These are modest gains; the methods, proofs, and quantitative evidence remain unchanged, and the replacement qualitative examples do not establish a performance improvement.
